Step 2: Check — The shelf was marked restricted and no curator was present, so both conditions of restricted shelf status are met. [Rule 2]. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Unauthorized stack entry (step 1) occurred in the restricted shelf area (step 2), so a restricted shelf violation is established. [Rule 8]. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — The relic was tagged fragile and Casey lifted it from its cradle, which is one of the listed conditions for fragile relic handling. [Rule 3]. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — The restricted shelf violation (step 3) combined with fragile relic handling (step 4) establishes a relic handling violation. [Rule 9]. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Casey had a written curator order, the order named the relic, and the handling time was logged; all three conditions for complete curator authorization records are met. [Rule 6]. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Check — The relic handling (step 5) is supported by complete curator authorization records (step 6), so curator order authorization is established. [Rule 12]. Result: PASS.
Step 8: Check — The catalog lock was not active, so catalog record interference conditions cannot be met; no catalog alteration violation arises.. Result: FAIL.
Step 9: Check — The exit alarm was not active, so no vault exit step is present and vault removal cannot be established.. Result: FAIL.
Step 10: Check — No flood alarm sounded, so flood rescue records cannot be complete and flood rescue authorization is not established.. Result: FAIL.
Step 11: Check — The relic handling violation (step 5) triggers the relic handling breach article, which prescribes reading room suspension. [Rule 15]. Result: PASS.
Step 12: Check — The restricted shelf access article also applies to the restricted shelf violation (step 3); where both apply, the relic handling breach article prevails. [Rule 20]. Result: PASS.
Step 13: Check — Curator order authorization (step 7) operates as an exception to the relic handling breach article when both apply; the exception applies and displaces the suspension. [Rule 26]. Result: PASS.
Step 14: Conclusion — The curator order authorization article applies as an exception to the prevailing relic handling breach article, and its prescribed consequence is no criminal liability. Flood rescue authorization does not apply, and no other violation (catalog alteration or vault removal) is established. [Rule 18]. Result: No criminal liability.

Step 1: Check — expense type: the packet covers graduate thesis review/defense fees, lecture fees, and expert consulting fees, which fall under the 'Remuneration Declaration' business type (Rule 1) and are governed by the labor service fee standards (Rule 13). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — thesis level classification: the thesis item is not marked as doctoral and is recorded as a master's thesis, so the master's standards of Rule 13(1) apply (2-3 reviewers at 200-300; 3-5 defense committee members at 200-300; 1 defense secretary at 100). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Compute — thesis review/defense fees: 2 reviewers × 250 = 500 (count 2 within 2-3, rate 250 within 200-300); 3 committee members × 250 = 750 (count 3 within 3-5, rate 250 within 200-300); 1 secretary × 100 = 100 (matches the master's secretary standard). Subtotal = 500 + 750 + 100. Result: 1350.
Step 4: Check — lecture fee rate: the academician-level cap is 1,500 per class hour (after tax); the recorded 1,500 per class hour does not exceed the cap. The standard is not marked as after tax, so per Rule 13(2) it should be confirmed/declared as an after-tax amount, but the amount stays within the cap under either reading. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Compute — lecture fee total: 1,500 × 4 class hours = 6,000; 4 class hours within 1 half-day equals the maximum of 4 class hours per half day, which is allowed, and there is no repeated calculation across classes (1 session). Result: 6000.
Step 6: Check — consultation categorization: the participant is bureau-director-level, which corresponds to professor-level (full senior title) rank under the university's rank mapping (Rule 7 lists professors within bureau-director-level personnel), so the 'senior professional technical titles or equivalent' on-site standard applies: 500-800 per person/day for days 1-2 and 300-400 per person/day from day 3 onward. The consultation is in person (on-site, not written/remote) and the per-project fee is 0, so only the daily rates apply. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Compute — consultation fee: claimed 3 days × 450 = 1,350. Days 1-2: 450 ≤ 800 cap, compliant. Day 3: 450 > 400 cap → excess of 50 for 1 day = 50 not reimbursable; reimbursable consultation = 1,350 − 50. Result: 1300.
Step 8: Compute — packet totals: claimed 1,350 + 6,000 + 1,350 = 8,700; reimbursable 1,350 + 6,000 + 1,300 = 8,650; excluded amount 50 (day-3 consultation fee exceeding the 400 cap). Result: 8650.
Step 9: Conclusion — thesis review/defense fees fully comply with the master's standards; the lecture fee is within the academician cap and the half-day class-hour limit (with the after-tax basis to be confirmed per Rule 13(2)); the day-3 consultation fee exceeds the standard cap and must be excluded before reimbursement. Result: Partially reimbursable.

Step 1: Check — Expense type identification: case involves office stationery, books, printing, and monograph publication subsidy, matching Rule 6's scope and Rule 1's regular reimbursement category. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Rule 6(2) low-value consumables not in Asset Management Office review scope: seller goods list was provided (no online purchase record required since a goods list suffices); Asset Management Office review correctly deemed not required. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Rule 6(3) book detailed list: no detailed list for book-related expense was provided; the rule states book expenses shall generally be accompanied by a detailed list. Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Check — Rule 6(3) and Rule 16(1) fixed-asset book registration: at least one single book is priced at RMB 1,000 or above, which requires registration with the Humanities and Social Sciences Library and a fixed asset addition form; no library registration and no fixed-asset addition slip were attached. Result: FAIL.
Step 5: Check — Rule 6(5) printing detailed list requirement: no single printing invoice exceeded RMB 1,000 and no same-period printing invoices together exceeded RMB 1,000, so no detailed list is required; no artificial splitting was detected. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Rule 6(6) monograph publication subsidy: requires the original or a copy of the publishing contract; no contract was included, so the subsidy cannot be verified or reimbursed. The counterparty designation and approval signatures are moot because the contract itself is missing. Result: FAIL.
Step 7: Compute — Reimbursable portion: office stationery (with seller goods list) and printing expenses (below the 1,000 list threshold, no splitting) are compliant; book expenses (missing detailed list, missing library registration/fixed-asset form for a book ≥ RMB 1,000) and the monograph publication subsidy (missing publishing contract) are non-compliant. Result: 2 of 4 categories compliant.
Step 8: Conclusion — The package is partly compliant: stationery and printing items meet Rule 6 requirements, but the book expense fails Rule 6(3)/Rule 16(1) (detailed list and library registration/fixed-asset form missing for a book at RMB 1,000+) and the monograph publication subsidy fails Rule 6(6) (no publishing contract). These non-compliant portions must be excluded or supplemented before reimbursement. Result: Partially reimbursable.

Step 1: Check — Identify expense type: organized training series with trainees, instructor fees, accommodation, meals, venue/materials/transport, and training-expense list. Result: PASS — Training Expenses (Rule 10).
Step 2: Check — Training duration control under Rule 10(2): 20 days ≤ 30 days, excess days = 0. Result: PASS — full comprehensive quota standard applies, no 70% reduction on excess days.
Step 3: Check — Required materials under Rule 10(3): training-expense detailed list, trainee list with contact information, and service-provider receipts. Result: PASS — all attached.
Step 4: Check — Trainee rank category: national management post grade 2 or above maps to the highest category; file quota references (500/150/80/30, total 760) match the ministerial-level-and-equivalent standard in Rule 10(1). Result: PASS — applicable quota total is 760 per person per day.
Step 5: Compute — Comprehensive quota ceiling for main training and comparison with claimed items. Result: 760 × 20 = 15,200; claimed 10,000 + 3,000 + 1,600 + 600 = 15,200; each item exactly at its per-day standard × 20 days, nothing exceeds; 15,200 fully allowed.
Step 6: Check — Instructor fees under Rule 10(4): excluded from comprehensive quota; lecture fee 2,000 checked against Rule 13(2) standards; instructor accommodation 700, meals 150, and inter-city transportation 800 (from another location) checked against applicable standards. Result: PASS — no demonstrable excess (title/class hours and instructor stay days not stated, no basis to reduce).
Step 7: Compute — Instructor fees total. Result: 2,000 + 700 + 150 + 800 = 3,650.
Step 8: Compute — Final reimbursable total. Result: 15,200 + 3,650 = 18,850.
Step 9: Conclusion — All claimed items comply with or do not demonstrably exceed the applicable rules; the full claimed amount is reimbursable. Result: Reimbursable — 18,850 CNY.

Step 1: Check — Expense type identification: the claim covers a training series with accommodation, meals, venue/materials/transportation, other expenses and instructor fees, plus a training-expense detailed list, trainee list and service-provider receipts, matching Rule 10 'Reimbursement of Training Expenses'. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Duration threshold under Rule 10(2): the training lasted 12 days with 0 days beyond the 30-day threshold, so the full comprehensive quota standard applies (no 70% adjustment for excess days is needed). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Applicable quota tier: trainees are at national management post level two or above, which falls in the ministerial-level and equivalent tier whose comprehensive quota is accommodation 500, meals 150, venue/materials/transportation 80, other 30, total 760 per person per day; this matches the quota references recorded in the file. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Compute — Per-person-per-day training expenses over 12 days: accommodation 6000/12 = 500; meals 1800/12 = 150; venue/materials/transportation 900/12 = 75; other 360/12 = 30; total 9060/12 = 755 (12-day per-person total 9060 vs quota 760 x 12 = 9120). Result: 755.
Step 5: Check — Item-by-item quota comparison: 500 <= 500, 150 <= 150, 75 <= 80, 30 <= 30, and total 755 <= 760; since amounts for different items may be adjusted among themselves under total amount control, all main training expenses are within the comprehensive quota. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Separate treatment of instructor fees under Rule 10(4): instructor costs (lecture fee 2000, accommodation 500, meals 150, inter-city transportation 300) are listed separately from the 9060 quota-covered training total, consistent with the requirement that instructor fees are calculated separately and not included in the comprehensive quota. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Check — Instructor lecture fee against labor service lecture-fee standards (Rule 13): 2000 is within the per-class-hour ceilings (<=500 associate senior, <=1000 full senior, <=1500 academician, max 4 class hours per half day) for the class hours delivered; no exceeding indicated. Result: PASS.
Step 8: Check — Instructor accommodation and meals against the training comprehensive quota standards per Rule 10(4): 500 <= 500 and 150 <= 150. Result: PASS.
Step 9: Check — Instructor inter-city transportation: the instructor came from another location, and the 300 transportation cost follows the travel expense standards referenced by Rule 10(4); no violation indicated. Result: PASS.
Step 10: Check — Training-specific materials under Rule 10(3): training-expense detailed list attached, trainee list with contact information attached, and training service-provider receipts attached; all three required materials are present. Result: PASS.
Step 11: Check — General material requirements under Rule 3: the reimbursement packet was compiled by handling staff member Dr. Xu with the listed attachments, and no missing form, signature, or invoice deficiency is indicated. Result: PASS.
Step 12: Conclusion — Training duration within 30 days, the correct ministerial-level quota tier applied with all training items at or below the comprehensive quota, instructor fees separately calculated and within applicable standards, and all required materials attached; the claim complies with the rules. Result: Fully reimbursable.

Step 1: Check — Whether the business falls under circumstances allowed for a temporary loan under Rule 20(1): the case is a special business item where an invoice could not be obtained in advance. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the borrower meets the eligible identity categories under Rule 20(2): borrower must be a Fudan University employee on the payroll, a leased employee with an R- or L-prefixed employee number, or a postdoctoral researcher; the case marks the borrower as none of these three categories. Result: FAIL.
Step 3: Check — Whether the borrower belongs to a category explicitly prohibited by Rule 20(3): the case marks the borrower as a student, and students may not act as borrowers for temporary loan business. Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Check — Whether the borrower signed the 'Fudan University Reservation Reimbursement Form' for confirmation as required by Rule 20(2): the case states the borrower signed the form. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Compute — Write-off timing under Rule 20(4): same-city settlement requires write-off generally within 30 days; recorded days until write-off are 20, and 20 <= 30. Result: 20.
Step 6: Check — Prior-loan status under Rule 20(5): the borrower has no outstanding unwritten-off loan, so there is no bar to accepting a new loan application. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Conclusion — Although the business need (Rule 20(1)), signature confirmation, write-off timing, and prior-loan status all satisfy Rule 20, the borrower is a student and is not identified as any eligible borrower category, so the application fails the borrower-identity requirements of Rule 20(2) and (3) and cannot be approved. Result: Ineligible for temporary loan.

Step 1: Check — Expense type identification: the spending categories are office stationery/consumables, books, and search/retrieval fees; Rule 6(1) places stationery and books under office expenses and Rule 6(4) charges novelty search and retrieval fees under printing expenses, so the case is an office expenses and printing expenses reimbursement. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Rule 6(2) documentation for the low-value consumable purchase: the purchase is outside the Asset Management Office review scope, so a seller goods list OR an online purchase transaction record must be attached; a seller goods list was provided, so the disjunctive requirement is satisfied even though no online transaction record and no Purchased Inventory Review Result Confirmation Form were attached (the latter is only required when AMO review applies). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Rule 6(3) fixed-asset threshold for books: no single book item is marked at RMB 1,000 or above, so registration with the Humanities and Social Sciences Library and a fixed-asset addition form are not triggered; the books' non-registration with the library is therefore not a deficiency. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Rule 6(3) detailed-list requirement for books: book and reference material expenses shall generally be accompanied by a detailed list, and the case confirms no detailed list for the book-related expense was provided. Result: FAIL.
Step 5: Check — Rule 6(4)/(5) printing-related items: search and retrieval fees are correctly charged under printing expenses; no single printing invoice exceeded RMB 1,000, no same-period printing invoices together exceeded RMB 1,000, no printing detailed list is therefore required, and the invoice amounts were not artificially split. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Rule 6(6) monograph-publication contract control: no monograph publication subsidy is claimed in this packet, so the requirement for an original or copy of the publishing contract (and any project-fund administrator approval thereon) is not applicable. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Compute — Share of expense categories whose documentation fully satisfies Rule 6: office stationery/consumables (seller goods list provided) and printing-related search/retrieval fees are compliant, while the book expense is deficient — 2 of 3 categories compliant (≈66.7%). Result: 2 of 3 (≈66.7%).
Step 8: Conclusion — The office stationery/consumables portion (supported by the seller goods list) and the printing-related search/retrieal fees satisfy Rule 6 and the general material framework and are reimbursable; however, the book-related expense lacks the detailed list required by Rule 6(3) and must be supplemented with a detailed list or excluded before reimbursement, so the packet as a whole is only partially reimbursable. Result: Partially reimbursable.

Step 1: Check — Whether the purchase falls within the Asset Management Office review scope for purchased inventory (Rule 6(2)): the purchase was not treated as a low-value consumable requiring review, and no review form was required. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether sufficient supporting documentation exists for out-of-scope office supplies (Rule 6(2)): a seller goods list was provided, which satisfies the requirement; no online purchase record is needed when a goods list exists. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether fixed-asset registration is required for books (Rule 6(3)): no single book item was priced at RMB 1,000 or above, so registration with the library and a fixed-asset addition form are not required; their absence is acceptable. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Whether a detailed list for book expenses is required (Rule 6(3)): the rule states book expenses shall 'generally' be accompanied by a detailed list; no single book reached RMB 1,000, and given the 'generally' qualifier this is not a mandatory item, so its absence does not block reimbursement. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Whether a detailed list for printing expenses is required (Rule 6(5)): no single printing invoice exceeded RMB 1,000, no multiple near-time printing invoices together exceeded RMB 1,000, and no artificial splitting was observed, so no detailed list is required. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Whether a monograph-publication contract is required (Rule 6(6)): no monograph-publication subsidy expense appears in the package; there is no monograph contract, no individual/department counterparty, and no project-fund administrator approval needed, indicating no monograph subsidy is being claimed. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Check — Whether general material requirements under Rule 3 are met: the reimbursement was properly reserved and organized as a regular reimbursement business, and no missing mandatory approvals, signatures, or invoices are indicated. Result: PASS.
Step 8: Conclusion — All business-specific requirements of Rule 6 are satisfied: goods list provided for office supplies, no asset review needed, books below registration threshold, printing below list threshold without splitting, and no monograph subsidy requiring a contract. The package contains no violations or missing mandatory materials. Result: Fully reimbursable.

Step 1: Check — Determine expense type: the case involves supplies (low-value consumables), books, printing invoices, and monograph-publication support, which map to Rule 6 (office expenses, books, printing expenses, monograph publication subsidies). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Rule 6(2): the purchase was treated as a low-value consumable outside the Asset Management Office review scope; a seller goods list was provided (acceptable substitute for the online purchase transaction record). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Rule 6(3): the book expense has a detailed list, but at least one single book is priced at RMB 1,000 or above. The rule requires registration with the Humanities and Social Sciences Library AND obtaining a fixed asset addition form. Library registration was completed, but no fixed-asset addition slip was attached. Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Check — Rule 6(5): no single printing invoice exceeds RMB 1,000 and no multiple near-time printing invoices together exceed RMB 1,000, so no detailed list is required; amounts were not artificially split. Printing portion complies. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Rule 6(6): a monograph publication subsidy shall be supported by the original or copy of the publishing contract. No monograph-publication contract was included in the package. Result: FAIL.
Step 6: Check — Rule 16(1)/16(3): books are registered with the library per Rule 16(1); the consumable purchase was treated as low-value consumables rather than purchased materials requiring the Purchased Inventory Confirmation Form, consistent with the treatment stated in the case. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Compute — Portion analysis: low-value consumable supplies (with seller goods list) = compliant; books with detail list and library registration = compliant except the RMB 1,000+ book item missing the fixed-asset addition form; printing expenses (no invoice/aggregate above RMB 1,000) = compliant; monograph-publication subsidy = non-compliant due to missing publishing contract. Result: 2 non-compliant items, 2 compliant items.
Step 8: Conclusion — The reimbursement package is partly compliant: the supplies, printing, and compliant book portions may be reimbursed, but (1) the RMB 1,000+ book item must be supplemented with the fixed-asset addition form or excluded, and (2) the monograph-publication subsidy portion cannot be reimbursed without the publishing contract (and required approvals if the counterparty is an individual or department). The case therefore requires partial exclusion/supplementation before reimbursement. Result: Partially reimbursable.

Step 1: Check — Rule 3(1): printed reservation reimbursement form submitted, fund booklet accounting entry copy submitted, form bears project leader's and handler's signatures, and project leader matches the financial system record. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Rule 3(1) authorization exception: a separate authorization letter is only required if the project leader cannot sign for special reasons; here the project leader signed the form directly, so no authorization letter is needed. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Rule 3(2): original invoices bear signatures of both the project leader and the handler. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Rule 3(2): for university-allocated funds, the designated single-signature approver signed; research-project PI signature is only required for research project funds, and this is a university-allocated fund matter, so absence of a research PI signature as the approval basis is not a deficiency; the matter is not special business requiring department approval, so no department approval is needed. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Rule 3(2) electronic invoice clause: the invoice is not an electronic invoice, so system-side authentication and selection of an electronic invoice in the reservation system are not applicable. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Rule 3(3): the packet involves no travel, overseas travel, conference expenses, equipment purchase, or research fund transfer, so the corresponding approvals, documents, reports, and explanatory notes are not required. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Compute — payment amount threshold check: payment is below RMB 30,000, so a signed contract with Fudan University's contract seal is not mandatory; nevertheless a signed contract bearing the university seal was included, and since a construction contract is attached, the construction-expenditure contract requirement under Rule 3(4) is also satisfied regardless of amount. Result: 29999 (below 30000).
Step 8: Check — Rule 3(5): payment does not exceed RMB 50,000, so the 'Fudan University Application Form for Large Cash Fund Payments' with unit-head signature and official seal is not required; its absence is therefore not a deficiency. Result: PASS.
Step 9: Conclusion — all mandatory materials under Rule 3 are present or not applicable; absent items (authorization letter, research PI approval signature, department special-business approval, electronic invoice authentication, business-type approvals, large-sum payment form) are only required under conditions that do not apply to this case, and the contract materials present exceed the requirements. Result: Materials complete.

Step 1: Check — whether office stationery purchases within the Asset Management Office review scope have the 'Fudan University Purchased Inventory Review Result Confirmation Form' (Rule 6(2)); case states Asset Management Office review was not required, and for items outside the review scope a seller goods list or online purchase record suffices. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — whether a seller goods list or online purchase transaction record is attached for non-review-scope office supplies; case states a seller goods list was provided. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — whether book and reference material expenses are accompanied by a detailed list (Rule 6(3)); case states no detailed list for book-related expense was provided. Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Check — whether any single book reached RMB 1,000 or above requiring library registration and a fixed asset addition form (Rule 6(3)); case states no single book item was marked at RMB 1,000 or above, so registration is not triggered; however the base detailed-list requirement still fails. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — whether a detailed list is required for printing expenses (Rule 6(5), required only when a single invoice or same-period invoices total more than RMB 1,000); case states no single printing invoice exceeded RMB 1,000, no multiple near-time invoices together exceeded RMB 1,000, and no artificial splitting occurred, so the list is not required. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — whether a monograph publication subsidy is claimed requiring a publishing contract (Rule 6(6)); the spending categories in the file only include office stationery, and the case shows no monograph publication subsidy claim; the contract counterparty is not marked as an individual or department, so the additional project-fund administrator approval condition is also not triggered. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Compute — aggregate compliance across the package: office stationery portion complies (goods list attached), printing portion complies (below list threshold, no splitting), monograph contract condition not applicable; only the book expense portion lacks its required detailed list. Result: 1 non-compliant item.
Step 8: Conclusion — the office stationery and printing portions satisfy Rule 6 requirements and are reimbursable, but the book expense portion is missing the required detailed list under Rule 6(3) and must be excluded or supplemented before reimbursement; therefore the package is partially reimbursable. Result: Partially reimbursable.

[Object : Training session coordinated by Teacher Wu (trainees: Major National Research Project Leaders)]
Step 1: Check — Expense type is training expenses (thematic training sessions with trainee quota items and instructor fees), so Rule 10 applies. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Training duration is 5 days, within the 30-day comprehensive quota control under Rule 10(2). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Trainees are Major National Research Project Leaders; under Rule 7(2), principal investigators of major research projects belong to the highest personnel class, mapping to the Rule 10 quota category 'Personnel at ministerial level and equivalent' (total 760 RMB/person/day). Result: PASS.
Step 4: Compute — 5-day comprehensive quota for ministerial-level and equivalent: accommodation 500×5=2,500; meals 150×5=750; venue/materials/transportation 80×5=400; other expenses 30×5=150; total 760×5=3,800 RMB. Result: 3800.
Step 5: Check — Rule 10(1) allows amounts to be adjusted among items with total amount control; claimed total 2,500+750+400+230=3,880 RMB exceeds the 3,800 RMB quota (other expenses of 230 exceed the 150 standard and push the total over the cap) by 80 RMB. Result: FAIL.
Step 6: Check — Required materials under Rule 10(3): the Fudan University Training Expense Detailed List is included for Wu's session; trainee roster with contact information and itemized receipts from the training service provider are included. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Check — Instructor fee per Rule 10(4) and Rule 13(2): lecture fee of 1,000 RMB with written approval for the elevated standard, calculated separately and not included in the comprehensive quota (1,000 RMB does not exceed the per-class-hour caps for full-senior professionals at 1,000 or academicians/renowned experts at 1,500, though per-class-hour details are not provided); instructor accommodation 500 and meals 150 do not exceed the ministerial-level quota standard; instructor inter-city transportation 300 RMB falls under Rule 7 with no evident violation. Result: PASS.
Step 8: Conclusion — Materials and instructor-fee requirements are met, but the trainee-side total exceeds the comprehensive quota by 80 RMB, which must be excluded before reimbursement. Result: Partially reimbursable.

[Object : Training session coordinated by Teacher Chen (trainees: national professional-technical post level 2 personnel)]
Step 1: Check — Expense type is training expenses; Rule 10 applies. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Training duration is 5 days, within the 30-day quota control under Rule 10(2). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Trainees are national professional-technical post level 2 personnel; under Rule 7(2) they belong to the highest personnel class, mapping to the Rule 10 quota category 'Personnel at ministerial level and equivalent' (total 760 RMB/person/day). Result: PASS.
Step 4: Compute — 5-day comprehensive quota: accommodation 500×5=2,500; meals 150×5=750; venue/materials/transportation 80×5=400; other expenses 30×5=150; total 3,800 RMB. Result: 3800.
Step 5: Check — Claimed total 2,500+750+400+150=3,800 RMB equals the quota; within total amount control under Rule 10(1). Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Required materials under Rule 10(3): trainee roster with contact information and itemized receipts from the training service provider are included, but the required 'Fudan University Training Expense Detailed List' (approved by the relevant school/department) is missing for Chen's session (only Wu, Tang, and Han included it). Result: FAIL.
Step 7: Check — Instructor fee per Rule 10(4)/Rule 13(2): lecture fee 1,000 RMB with written approval, outside the comprehensive quota; instructor accommodation 500 and meals 150 within the ministerial-level standard; inter-city transportation 300 RMB under Rule 7, no evident violation. Result: PASS.
Step 8: Conclusion — An essential required material under Rule 10(3) is missing; the reimbursement cannot be approved until the Training Expense Detailed List is supplied. Result: Not reimbursable.

[Object : Training session coordinated by Teacher Tang (trainees: academician-level participants)]
Step 1: Check — Expense type is training expenses; Rule 10 applies. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Training duration is 5 days, within the 30-day quota control under Rule 10(2). Result: PASS.

Result: PASS.

[Object : Training session coordinated by Teacher Han (trainees: national ministry/bureau-level or above management personnel)]
Step 1: Check — Expense type is training expenses; Rule 10 applies. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Training duration is 5 days, within the 30-day quota control under Rule 10(2). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Trainees are ministry/bureau-level or above management personnel; the group includes ministerial-level personnel, so the highest Rule 10 quota category 'Personnel at ministerial level and equivalent' (total 760 RMB/person/day) applies; the instructor's ancillary accommodation of 500 and meals of 150 also correspond to this category's standard. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Compute — 5-day comprehensive quota: accommodation 500×5=2,500; meals 150×5=750; venue/materials/transportation 80×5=400; other expenses 30×5=150; total 3,800 RMB. Result: 3800.
Step 5: Check — Rule 10(1) allows adjustment among items with total amount control; claimed total 2,500+750+400+230=3,880 RMB exceeds the 3,800 RMB quota (other expenses of 230 exceed the 150 standard) by 80 RMB. Result: FAIL.
Step 6: Check — Required materials under Rule 10(3): Fudan University Training Expense Detailed List included for Han's session; trainee roster with contact information and itemized receipts from the training service provider included. Result: PASS.
